iteration: Planning round number for this case. Integer starting at 1.

case.paper_file: File name or local path of the original paper PDF.
case.focal_claim: Exact focal claim under test. No agent may change this.
case.hypothesis: Focal hypothesis phrased as a testable statement at the level of operationalized variables.

tasks_info.task_instruction: Assigned instruction for Task1. Example: Conduct the analysis without any restrictions.
tasks_info.task_goal: Test whether the focal claim is supported.

tasks_info.task_instruction: Assigned instruction for Task2, including all case-specific constraints.
tasks_info.task_goal: Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

datasets.authorized_only: true. No agent may substitute a dataset not listed here.
datasets.source_type: Data source, such as survey, experiment, database, or archive.
datasets.wave_or_subset: Specific waves, subsets, or sample restrictions, if applicable.
datasets.sample_size: Expected analytic sample size if known, otherwise not_stated.
datasets.unit_of_analysis: Unit of analysis, such as individual, household, country, firm, or trial.
datasets.notes: Caveats about the data: encoding issues, nested structure, missing metadata, unusual column formats.

files.name: Dataset name. Example: RiskData.
files.file_path: Local path to the data file.
files.file_format: csv, dta, rdata, rds, xlsx, json, parquet, or other.
columns: Key variable names if available, otherwise not_stated.

summary_statistics.describe: Compact descriptive statistics for focal variables, or null.

files.access_details: Local path, repository link, access restriction, or not_stated.

plan.planned_id: Unique ID for this planned path. Example: Bruner_ExpEco_2017_amYY_path04.
plan.path_summary: Short summary of the proposed analysis path.

path_signature.model_family: Main model or test family. Example: linear_regression, logistic_regression, correlation, t_test, poisson, multilevel, Bayesian.
path_signature.main_predictor: Main predictor, treatment, or grouping variable.
controls: List of control variables, or empty list.
path_signature.sample_restriction: Sample inclusion or exclusion rule, or null.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Missing data handling rule, or null.
path_signature.variable_construction: How the main variables are created or changed before analysis, or null.
path_signature.inference_rule: How the result will be judged.

analysis_path.path_name: Short name for the path. Example: linear_regression_risk_aversion_decision_error.
analysis_path.path_description: Concise description of what should be run for this task.
analysis_path.software: Software or language used. Example: R, Stata, Matlab, Python, or not_stated.
analysis_path.original_software: Language of the original analysis code, if it differs from software.
analysis_path.model_family: Main model or test family for this task.
preprocessing_steps: Ordered preprocessing and preparation steps. Another analyst should be able to reconstruct the code from this list.

key_choices.outcome_measure: How the outcome is measured or constructed.
key_choices.main_predictor_measure: How the main predictor is measured or constructed.
control_variables: Control variable names, or empty list.
key_choices.sample_restriction: Sample inclusion or exclusion rule, or null.
key_choices.data_processing: Any reshaping, recoding, aggregation, scaling, or transformation.
key_choices.model_choice: Main model or statistical test used.
key_choices.inference_rule: Rule used to judge support. Example: expected direction and p < 0.05.

models.model_id: Unique model ID within this task. Example: M1.
models.type: Model or statistical approach. Example: linear regression, t-test.
models.formula: Explicit model specification when expressible. Example: lndrate ~ b10_10 * factor(decade_two) + yearmo + year2. Use null if not applicable.
models.planned_estimation: Main quantity to estimate. Example: coefficient, mean difference, odds ratio, correlation.
models.inference_criteria: Rule for judging this model's result.
models.deviation: true if this uses a meaningfully different choice from the original paper, otherwise false.
models.qualification: Why this is a valid design choice to test the focal claim, especially when it deviates from the original paper.

outcome.name: Outcome variable name or constructed outcome name.
outcome.definition: What the variable means and how it is operationalized and mathematically formulated.
outcome.variable_construction: How this variable is created, recoded, scaled, transformed, or aggregated. Use null if the raw variable is used.
outcome.missing_data_handling: Rule for missing data on this variable.
outcome.deviation: true if this uses a meaningfully different choice from the original paper, otherwise false.
outcome.qualification: Why this variable choice is valid for the focal claim.
models: model_id values that use this variable.

main_predictor.name: Main predictor variable name.
main_predictor.definition: What the variable means and how it is operationalized.
main_predictor.missing_data_handling: Rule for missing data on this variable.
main_predictor.qualification: Why this variable choice is valid for the focal claim.
models: model_id values that use this variable.

controls.name: Control variable name.
controls.missing_data_handling: Rule for missing data, or null.
controls.qualification: Why this control is appropriate, or null.
models: model_id values that use this variable.

expected_outputs: What this task should produce. Example: OLS model summaries, interaction plot.

analysis_code.available: true if analysis code for this task exists; false otherwise.
code_files: Files needed for this specific task.
analysis_code.entry_file: Main script to run for this task, or null.
analysis_code.run_command: Command to run this task, or null.
analysis_code.notes: Task-specific notes about running the analysis code.

tasks.notes_for_agent: Task-specific rule. Example: Follow this planned path; do not change the focal claim, dataset, or analysis goal.

plan.tools_software: Software or tools expected for execution, such as R, Python, Stata, or specific packages.

method_justification.claim_alignment: How this path tests the same focal claim.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: How this path uses the authorized original dataset.
method_justification.method_reason: Why the models, variables, and inference rule are reasonable for the claim.
method_justification.novelty_reason: Why this path differs from paths already in shared_memory.

self_check.self_check_note: Short explanation of the self check.

docker_specs.base_image: Base Docker image containing the software needed to run the analysis. Example: python:3.10, rocker/verse.

python: Required Python packages with version constraints. Example: pandas>=1.4.0.
other: Other necessary software. Example: git, make, wget.

hardware.gpu_support: true if a GPU is required, false otherwise.
hardware.min_gpu_memory_gb: Minimum GPU memory in GB, or null.

volumes: Host paths to mount inside the container. Example: ./data:/app/data.

execution_directives.instructions: High-level execution instruction. Example: Execute Task1 and Task2 using the original dataset and produce structured execution outputs.
target_task_ids: Task IDs to execute. Example: Task1, Task2.

debugging_rule.repair_scope: Allowed repair scope. Example: fix dependency, file path, or output extraction issues only; do not redesign the analysis.

execution_directives.comparison_metrics: Expected metrics or outputs for later comparison. Example: coefficient, p-value, test statistic, Cohen's d, conclusion text.
